body:
Complete guide to Pokémon Legends: Arceus. Learn about Alpha Pokémon, Noble battles, space-time distortions, and how to complete the first Pokédex in the Hisui region.

Pokémon Legends: Arceus revolutionized the Pokémon franchise with its open-world design, action-oriented gameplay, and emphasis on research and exploration. Set in the ancient Hisui region (the predecessor to modern Sinnoh), the game challenges players to complete the first ever Pokédex. This guide covers everything you need to master this unique adventure.

Table of Contents

  1. Getting Started in Hisui
  2. Completing the Pokédex
  3. Alpha Pokémon
  4. Noble Pokémon Battles
  5. Space-Time Distortions
  6. Best Pokémon to Catch
  7. Post-Game Content
  8. Conclusion

Getting Started in Hisui

Pokémon Legends: Arceus begins with your character joining the Galaxy Expedition Team in Jubilife Village. Unlike traditional Pokémon games, you do not choose your starter from a lab — instead, you receive your first Pokémon from Professor Laventon after a mysterious encounter. The three starters are Rowlet (Grass), Cyndaquil (Fire), and Oshawott (Water), all from previous generations.

The gameplay in Legends: Arceus is significantly different from mainline Pokémon games. You can move freely in the overworld, throw Poké Balls to catch wild Pokémon without battling, and gather materials for crafting. Battles still use the turn-based system, but with the addition of Strong and Agile styles that change move priority and power.

Early in the game, focus on completing research tasks for each Pokémon. These tasks include catching multiple specimens, seeing specific moves used, and evolving Pokémon. Completing research tasks increases your Survey Corps rank, which unlocks new items, areas, and abilities.

Completing the Pokédex

The Pokédex in Legends: Arceus is not completed simply by catching each Pokémon. To complete a Pokédex entry, you must reach Research Level 10 for each Pokémon by completing research tasks. These tasks include catching specimens, defeating them in battle, seeing them use specific moves, and more.

Some research tasks are worth more points than others. For example, catching a Pokémon might give you 1 point, but catching it with a specific technique (like a back strike) might give you 2 points. Evolving a Pokémon or seeing it use a strong move can also give multiple points. Focus on high-value tasks to complete entries efficiently.

Completing the Pokédex is a major time investment, but it is essential for progressing the story and unlocking the true ending of the game. As you complete entries, you will also learn more about each Pokémon behavior, habitat, and characteristics, making you a true Pokémon researcher.

Alpha Pokémon

Alpha Pokémon are a new feature in Legends: Arceus. These are larger, more powerful versions of regular Pokémon, with glowing red eyes and a distinctive roar. Alpha Pokémon have higher base stats than their regular counterparts, making them valuable additions to your team.

Alpha Pokémon can be found throughout the Hisui region, often in fixed locations. They are aggressive and will chase you if they spot you. To catch an Alpha Pokémon, you need to weaken it in battle and use a high-quality Poké Ball. Alpha Pokémon are worth more research points than regular Pokémon, making them valuable for Pokédex completion.

Some Alpha Pokémon are only available in specific areas or under certain conditions. For example, Alpha Pokémon in space-time distortions are often rare or powerful species. Catching Alpha Pokémon is one of the most rewarding experiences in the game, as they are both powerful and visually impressive.

Noble Pokémon Battles

Noble Pokémon are special, revered creatures that serve as the game boss battles. Unlike regular boss battles, Noble Pokémon battles are not traditional Pokémon fights. Instead, you must dodge their attacks in real-time, throw Balms to calm them, and use your Pokémon to battle when they are staggered.

There are five Noble Pokémon in the game: Kleavor, Lady Lilligant, Hisuian Arcanine, Hisuian Electrode, and Hisuian Avalugg. Each Noble has unique attack patterns and weaknesses. Learning their patterns and timing your dodges is essential for success.

After weakening a Noble with Balms, you can send out your Pokémon for a traditional battle. Defeating the Noble in battle staggers it, allowing you to throw more Balms. Repeat this process until the Noble is fully calmed. Noble battles are challenging but rewarding, and they advance the story significantly.

Space-Time Distortions

Space-time distortions are a late-game feature that introduces rare and powerful Pokémon to the Hisui region. These distortions appear randomly in the overworld and contain Pokémon from other regions and time periods. Inside a distortion, you can find rare Pokémon that are not available anywhere else in the game.

Distortions are indicated by a purple dome that appears on the map. Once you enter a distortion, you have a limited time to catch as many Pokémon as possible before the distortion closes. The Pokémon inside are often rare evolutions or species from other regions, making them valuable for Pokédex completion.

Some of the rarest Pokémon in the game, like starters from other generations and fossil Pokémon, can only be found in space-time distortions. If you see a distortion appear, drop everything and head to it immediately. You never know what rare Pokémon you might find inside.

Best Pokémon to Catch

Beyond your starter, there are several Pokémon in Hisui that are worth catching. Hisuian Growlithe evolves into Hisuian Arcanine, a Fire/Rock type with excellent all-around stats. Hisuian Zorua evolves into Hisuian Zoroark, a Normal/Ghost type with incredible special attack and three immunities.

Hisuian Sneasel evolves into Sneasler, a Poison/Fighting type with high Speed and Attack. Hisuian Qwilfish evolves into Overqwil, a Dark/Poison type with strong defensive typing. These Hisuian forms are unique to the game and cannot be found in other Pokémon games.

Other notable Pokémon include Garchomp, Garchomp is still one of the best pseudo-legendaries in the game. Togekiss provides excellent support with Serene Grace. Alpha Pokémon, especially those with good typing and stats, can carry you through the toughest battles.

For the post-game, you will want to catch the Creation Trio: Dialga, Palkia, and Giratina. These legendaries are essential for the final story battles and are among the most powerful Pokémon in the game. Arceus itself can be obtained by completing the Pokédex and returning to the Temple of Sinnoh.

Post-Game Content

After completing the main story, there is plenty of post-game content to enjoy. The story continues with the Search for the Plates, where you must find all 18 Plates scattered across Hisui. This quest takes you to new areas and introduces new challenges.

The final boss of the game, Arceus, is one of the most challenging battles in Pokémon history. Arceus is level 75 and has incredible stats across the board. Defeating Arceus is the ultimate test of your team and your skills as a trainer.

After defeating Arceus, you can catch it and add it to your team. Arceus is the only Pokémon that can use the move Judgment, which changes type based on the Plate it holds. Catching Arceus is the ultimate reward for completing the Pokédex and finishing the game.

Other post-game content includes the Eternal Battle Reverie, where you can battle against legendary Pokémon from across the franchise. This is a challenging gauntlet that tests your team to its limits, but it rewards you with rare items and the satisfaction of overcoming incredible odds.

Conclusion

Pokémon Legends: Arceus is a groundbreaking game that changed the Pokémon franchise forever. Its open-world design, action-oriented gameplay, and emphasis on research provide a fresh experience for veteran and new players alike. Completing the first Pokédex is a monumental task, but it is one of the most rewarding experiences in the franchise.

Use our random Pokémon generator to discover new Pokémon to research, and check our shiny Pokémon checker to see the shiny forms available in Hisui. The Hisui region is full of mysteries waiting to be uncovered — happy researching!

faq.q: How do you catch Arceus in Pokémon Legends Arceus?
faq.a: To catch Arceus, you must complete the entire Pokédex by catching or obtaining every Pokémon in the game, then complete the final mission at the Temple of Sinnoh.

faq.q: What are Noble Pokémon in Legends Arceus?
faq.a: Noble Pokémon are special Pokémon that have been blessed by the land. You battle them in special boss encounters where you must calm them down using Balms before battling them traditionally.

faq.q: How do you complete the Pokédex in Legends Arceus?
faq.a: Completing the Pokédex requires catching multiple of each species, seeing all their moves, and completing research tasks. This is more involved than simply catching one of each Pokémon.

faq.q: Is Pokémon Legends Arceus open world?
faq.a: Yes, Legends Arceus features semi-open world areas that you can explore freely. There are 5 main areas: Obsidian Fieldlands, Crimson Mirelands, Cobalt Coastlands, Coronet Highlands, and Alabaster Icelands.
